claims: IBM's illustration guidance recommends purpose, simplicity, essential elements and clear communication; it describes line, flat, and isometric illustration styles as listed in the supplied evidence.
Atlassian recommends meaningful illustrations that reflect user context and can explain tasks/workflows.
Claude Code skills can be understood as reusable procedural instructions added to Claude's toolkit and invoked automatically or directly.
Claude Code plugins package multiple components such as skills, subagents, hooks, and MCP servers as one unit.
Claude Code hooks are automatic actions at lifecycle points, while MCP connectors provide access to external tools, databases, and APIs.
WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.1.1 requires text alternatives equivalent in purpose for non-text content, including diagrams, with exceptions including decoration.
WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.3.3 bars instructions relying only on sensory characteristics such as color, shape, or location; labels can supplement these cues.
The W3C cognitive accessibility icon pattern is supplemental and recommends familiar, single-meaning icons adjacent to relevant content.

evidence.text: IBM Design Language illustration overview: Illustrations should have a clear purpose, support content, and guide users to understand difficult concepts, products or services. It recommends simplicity and essential, non-decorative elements. Its styles include line (precision, honesty, authority), flat (colorful, bold, graphic), and isometric (depth, space). https://www.ibm.com/design/language/illustration/overview/

Atlassian Design System illustrations guidance: illustrations help convey complex ideas simply; they should be meaningful and reflect users' context and emotional state. They can guide users through tasks, explain complex workflows, or provide context. https://atlassian.design/guidelines/brand/illustrations/

Claude Code skills documentation says skills are SKILL.md instructions added to Claude's toolkit; Claude uses them when relevant or users invoke directly; useful for repeat instructions, checklists, or multi-step procedures. Supporting files and project/plugin distribution also exist. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills

Claude Code plugin docs describe packaging several skills, subagents, hooks, or MCP servers in one unit; their example plugin combines a namespaced skill, subagent, lifecycle hooks and MCP tools. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins

Claude Code hooks are user-defined shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tool calls, LLM prompts, or subagents that execute automatically at specified lifecycle points. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks

Claude Code MCP docs say connected servers give access to tools, databases and APIs, letting Claude read and act on those systems directly. MCP's own introduction calls it an open-source standard connecting AI applications to external systems. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp

WCAG 2.2 Understanding 1.1.1 says all non-text content presented to users needs a text alternative serving equivalent purpose (with listed exceptions); charts, diagrams, pictures and animations can use short/long text alternatives; decoration can be ignored by AT. https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content

WCAG 2.1 Understanding 1.3.3: instructions must not rely solely on shape, color, size, location, orientation, or sound. Its example says an arrow is identified by label 'Next'; adding labels permits using color/position as additional cues. https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/sensory-characteristics.html

W3C Cognitive Accessibility design pattern 'Use Icons that Help the User' is supplemental guidance, not a WCAG requirement: add familiar icons/images/symbols to important content; each icon should convey a single meaning and sit near related content. https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG2/supplemental/patterns/o1p07-icons-used/

compare_runs.passage_a: IBM Design Language says illustration should have clear purpose, support understanding, be simple with essential non-decorative elements, and achieve an engineered, clear, nimble, diverse, delightful aesthetic. Styles include line, flat and isometric.
compare_runs.passage_b: Atlassian Design System says illustrations should simplify complex ideas, be meaningful and reflect user context and emotional state; they guide tasks and explain complex workflows, adding clarity and brand personality.
compare_runs.purpose: Reconcile official illustration-system guidance to identify overlap and differences useful to Found42 diagrams.
